destination.name: Sapphire Coast
destination.tagline: The far south coast of New South Wales, with long unspoilt beaches, national parks and the towns of Merimbula, Tathra and Eden.
destination.description: The Sapphire Coast is the southernmost coastal region on the east coast of Australia, in the far south-east of New South Wales. It is known for long, unspoilt beaches and is a common holiday spot for Victorians over summer and Easter. Bournda, Mimosa Rocks and Beowa national parks run along the shore, Tathra has a heritage wharf, and Eden's Killer Whale Museum shows Old Tom, the only complete orca skeleton on display in the Southern Hemisphere. Bega, inland, is famous for its cheese, and whale watching runs September to November.
whyVisit: Visit the Eden Killer Whale Museum

goodToKnow.title: Most beaches are unpatrolled
goodToKnow.detail: Check the water conditions before swimming; most beaches along the coast have no lifeguards and you swim at your own risk.

goodToKnow.title: Parks differ in cost
goodToKnow.detail: Bournda charges $8 per vehicle, while Mimosa Rocks is free.

goodToKnow.title: Fly in, then drive
goodToKnow.detail: Merimbula airport has flights from Sydney and Melbourne, but local buses run only a few services Monday to Friday, so a car suits the spread-out parks and towns.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: {months} are the warm months, with whale watching from September to November.
